# /style-bible

## Purpose

Decide how the comic is drawn and write it down in a form that can be
enforced. The style bible covers line, tone, texture, and rendering. The
color script covers palette and spot color scene by scene. The lettering
section covers font, case, and balloon shapes. The last output is the style
block: one paragraph of drawing instructions that is frozen and reused word
for word in every generation request, next to the look master image.

## Use When

- The story bible is approved and the look has to be fixed before any
  reference sheet is drawn.
- The user brings a style reference (run `/ingest-references` first) or
  picks a preset from `templates/looks/`.
- The look changes. That means a new look version and recompiled prompts,
  so do it before pages exist if at all possible.

## Inputs

- `look` (ID, optional): the `LOOK_*` ID to define, e.g. `LOOK_NOIR_INK`;
  default derived from the project's genre and influences.
- `preset` (string, optional): a preset file from `templates/looks/` to
  start from.
- `color_mode` (enum, optional, default from `project.yaml`): `monochrome` |
  `limited` | `full_color`.

## Invokes Agents

- art-director
- colorist
- letterer

## Required Skills

- visual-style-development
- color-scripting

## Process

1. Read the story bible's `tone`, the `style` and `color_mode` fields of
   `project.yaml`, any ingested look references in
   `production/references/manifest.yaml`, and the chosen preset.
2. art-director writes `production/style/style-bible.md`: line (weight,
   variation, contour), tone (how blacks and grays are placed), texture,
   rendering of faces and hands, and what the look refuses. Write each as a
   statement a reviewer can hold a page against.
3. colorist fixes `color_mode` and, for `limited`, the `spot_colors` in
   `project.yaml`, each with `name`, `hex`, and `use`. Then write
   `production/style/color-script.md`: palette and tonal progression per
   scene, and where a spot color is allowed to appear.
4. letterer writes the lettering section of the style bible and the
   `lettering` block of `project.yaml`: `font_family`, `case`,
   `max_words_per_balloon`, `max_words_per_panel`, balloon and caption
   shapes, and the treatment of sound effects. Confirm `lettering.mode`
   against the provider's `textRendering` capability.
5. Write `production/style/style-block.txt`: one paragraph of literal,
   model-facing drawing instructions taken from the style bible. Then
   freeze it. Every request reuses it verbatim, and a compiled prompt
   package records its hash in `source_hashes.style_block`.
6. Plan the look master, `LOOK_<NAME>_MASTER_V##`: a sample page in the
   style that `/visual-development` generates and the user approves. It is
   attached as an image, with the role `style`, to every request. A style
   word repeated in a prompt does not replace it.
7. Set `style.style_block` and `style.influences` in `project.yaml`. Leave
   `style.look_refs` empty until the look master is approved.
8. Run `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root production`, then the
   self-evaluation gates on the three style documents. Present the look for
   approval.

## Outputs

- `production/style/style-bible.md`, the visual language and lettering style
  (human document, no schema).
- `production/style/style-block.txt`, the frozen prompt block (model-facing
  text, no schema).
- `production/style/color-script.md`, palette per scene (human document, no
  schema).
- `production/project.yaml`, with `color_mode`, `spot_colors`, `lettering`,
  and `style` updated (`schemas/project.schema.json`).

## Notes

- No images are generated here, so the command is free.
- Editing the style block after pages exist changes its hash. Every prompt
  package compiled from the old text is stale and its pages no longer match
  the new ones. Treat that as a new look version, decided by the user.
- The style block is model-facing text. It is exempt from `/humanize` and
  answers to the `prompt-compilation` skill. The style bible and the color
  script are human documents and follow `rules/writing/prose-style.md`.
- Format differences: paged projects also read `rules/paged/print-specs.md`
  for trim and safe margins that lettering has to respect. Webtoon projects
  read `rules/webtoon/scroll-grammar.md` for vertical spacing between
  panels.
- Related: `/ingest-references` (before, when the user has material),
  `/visual-development` (draws the look master), `/lettering` (applies the
  lettering style).
